73748.e: Around 1900 Taylor studied work processes with a stopwatch and strictly separated planning from carrying out. It is also called Taylorism.
73748.m: Taylorism breaks work down into tiny steps.

73749.q: Which disadvantage is often linked to highly specialised assembly line work?
a: Too long training for each worker
73749.e: Anyone who always makes the same movement often suffers from boredom and one-sided physical strain. Karl Marx spoke of alienation from work.
73749.m: Strong specialisation can make work monotonous.

73750.q: Which form of work is meant to reduce monotony by having employees change workstations regularly?
73750.e: In job rotation employees switch between different tasks according to plan. This brings variety and broader knowledge.
73750.m: Job rotation brings variety through changing workstations.

73751.q: What does the economy-wide division of labour describe?
a: Specialisation of whole occupations and industries
Splitting one wage between two people
Dividing up holidays in a team
73751.e: In the economy-wide division of labour, people specialise in occupations and businesses in industries. They exchange their work through markets.
73751.m: In an economy, occupations and industries specialise.

73752.q: Which condition does an economy based on the division of labour absolutely need?
a: Exchange, usually through money and markets
73752.e: Anyone who specialises does not make everything themselves and must exchange their products for others. Money makes this exchange much easier.
73752.m: The division of labour only works with exchange.

73753.q: What is Toyota's way of producing, which avoids waste and delivers parts exactly when they are needed, called?
73753.e: The Toyota Production System is seen as the origin of lean management. Parts arrive just in time and stocks are kept small.
73753.m: Just in time saves storage but makes production vulnerable to disruption.

73754.q: Which single country was the second-largest exporter of clothing after China in 2023?
73754.e: According to the World Trade Organization, Bangladesh has followed China in clothing exports for years, ahead of Vietnam. The textile industry is its most important export sector.
73754.m: Bangladesh is a centre of global clothing production.

73755.q: Which disaster in Bangladesh, with over 1,100 deaths, led to worldwide debates about textile factories in 2013?
73755.e: On 24 April 2013 the Rana Plaza factory building near Dhaka collapsed and 1,134 people died. Afterwards an agreement on fire and building safety was created.
73755.m: Rana Plaza stands for the dangers of cheap textile production.

73756.q: Which raw material for a T-shirt needs especially large amounts of water to grow?
73756.e: Cotton is often irrigated artificially in dry areas. A single T-shirt can need several thousand litres of water. Flax for linen needs much less water.
73756.m: Growing cotton uses a great deal of water.

73757.q: Which lake in Central Asia has largely dried up, mainly because of irrigating cotton fields?
73757.e: Since the 1960s water has been diverted from the rivers feeding it, the Amu Darya and Syr Darya, for cotton. As a result the Aral Sea lost most of its area.
73757.m: The Aral Sea shrank because of cotton irrigation.

73758.q: Which country produces around three quarters of the world's mined cobalt, which is found in smartphone batteries (as of 2023)?
73758.e: According to the US Geological Survey, the DR Congo mined about three quarters of the world's cobalt in 2023. Small-scale mining and child labour there are criticised.
73758.m: Most cobalt for batteries comes from the DR Congo.

73759.q: Which Taiwanese company is known as the largest contract manufacturer, assembling iPhones among other things?
73759.e: Foxconn (Hon Hai Precision) assembles devices for many brands in large factories in China. It has been criticised several times over working conditions.
73759.m: Foxconn is the largest electronics contract manufacturer.

73760.q: Which country dominates the world's mining and processing of rare earths, which are needed in smartphones?
73760.e: China mines most of the rare earths and processes an even larger share. This creates dependence for the electronics industry.
73760.m: For rare earths, the world depends heavily on China.

73761.q: What is the most important reason why clothing is often sewn in countries like Bangladesh?
a: Low wage costs for labour-intensive sewing
73761.e: Sewing is hard to automate and needs a lot of manual work. That is why production pays off where wages are low.
73761.m: Labour-intensive production moves to countries with low wages.

73762.q: What is a business model in the fashion industry with very quickly changing, cheap collections called?
73762.e: Fast fashion brings new, cheap clothes into the shops every few weeks. Use of resources, waste and working conditions are criticised.
73762.m: Fast fashion means cheap clothing that changes quickly.

73763.q: Which crisis hit the Swiss watch industry hard in the 1970s and early 1980s?
73763.e: Cheap quartz watches from Japan and Hong Kong pushed out mechanical Swiss watches. The number of people working in the industry fell by more than half.
73763.m: The quartz crisis forced the watch industry to restructure.

73764.q: What does the term tertiarisation describe?
a: The growing importance of the service sector
73764.e: In tertiarisation, the share of services in employment and value added rises. This is typical of highly developed countries.
73764.m: Tertiarisation means the rise of services.

73765.q: What is the decline of industrial employment in a country or region called?
73765.e: Deindustrialisation describes the loss of industrial jobs, for example in the Ruhr area or in parts of eastern Switzerland with its former textile industry.

73766.q: Which industry particularly shaped eastern Switzerland in the 19th century but later declined sharply?
73766.e: Around 1900 St Gallen was a world centre of embroidery. After the First World War and changes in fashion, the industry collapsed.
73766.m: Eastern Switzerland once lived from embroidery.

73767.q: Which German region is an example of structural change away from coal and steel?
73767.e: In the Ruhr area, mines and blast furnaces were closed; hard coal mining ended in 2018. Today services, universities and culture shape the region.
73767.m: The Ruhr area changed from coal to services.

73768.q: What is meant by structural unemployment?
a: Unemployment because qualifications or industries do not match
A short search time between two jobs
73768.e: Structural unemployment arises when jobs disappear in shrinking industries and the people affected do not fit the new jobs.
73768.m: Structural change can lead to structural unemployment.

73769.q: Which tool works especially well in Switzerland to prepare employees for new occupations during structural change?
73769.e: Through further training, retraining and vocational education, employees can move into growing industries. Unemployment insurance supports such labour market measures.
73769.m: Further training prepares people for structural change.

73770.q: In which year did Henry Ford introduce the assembly line for building the Model T?
73770.e: In 1913 assembly at the Highland Park factory was switched to assembly line work. The time to assemble a car fell from over twelve hours to about one and a half.
73770.m: Ford's assembly line turned the car into a mass product.

73771.q: What were the English workers who destroyed textile machines from around 1811 to 1816 called?
73771.e: The Luddites protested against machines that devalued their work. Their name goes back to a legendary figure called Ned Ludd.

73772.q: Which event of 1832 is the best-known example of machine breaking in Switzerland?
73772.e: On 22 November 1832, home weavers and small farmers set fire to a mechanical weaving mill in Uster in the canton of Zurich. They feared for their income.
73772.m: The Uster fire was a protest against machine weaving.

73773.q: Which term describes connecting machines and products in a factory via the internet?
73773.e: The term Industry 4.0 became known in Germany in 2011. After the steam engine, the assembly line and the computer, it stands for the fourth industrial revolution.
73773.m: Industry 4.0 means the digitally connected factory.

73774.q: Which study estimated in 2013 that around 47 per cent of jobs in the USA could be at risk from computerisation?
a: The study by Frey and Osborne
73774.e: Carl Benedikt Frey and Michael Osborne from Oxford estimated the risk of automation for over 700 occupations. The figure was widely quoted and also criticised.
73774.m: Frey and Osborne started the debate about job losses through computers.

73775.q: Which country has had one of the highest robot densities in industry worldwide for years (as of 2023)?
73775.e: According to the International Federation of Robotics, South Korea has the highest robot density, with over 1,000 industrial robots per 10,000 industrial workers.
73775.m: South Korea uses a particularly large number of industrial robots.

73776.q: Which activities are considered especially easy to automate?
a: Creative tasks with lots of variety
Care work with lots of human contact
73776.e: Machines and software are especially good at taking over tasks that can be put into fixed rules. Social and creative work is harder to replace.
73776.m: Routine is easier to automate than creativity.

73777.q: Which weaving machine from around 1804 is seen as a forerunner of programming because it was controlled by punched cards?
73777.e: Joseph-Marie Jacquard controlled the patterns of his loom with punched cards. The principle later inspired early calculating machines.
73777.m: Jacquard's punched cards were an early program.

73778.q: What does the term technological unemployment mean?
a: Loss of jobs because technology replaces human work
Job losses because of high interest rates
73778.e: Technological unemployment arises when new technology makes work unnecessary. At the same time, history shows that new occupations often appear.
73778.m: Technology replaces jobs and creates new ones at the same time.

73779.q: How many hours of unpaid work were done in Switzerland in 2020, according to the Federal Statistical Office?
73779.e: The FSO recorded about 9.8 billion hours of unpaid work for 2020. That is more than the number of paid working hours.
73779.m: In Switzerland more work is unpaid than paid.

73780.q: Roughly what was the money value of unpaid work in Switzerland in 2020, according to the FSO?
73780.e: The household production satellite account valued unpaid work in 2020 at 434 billion francs. That is a very large sum compared with GDP.
73780.m: Unpaid work has a huge economic value.

73781.q: What share of unpaid work in Switzerland was done by women in 2020?
73781.e: According to the FSO, women did about 60 per cent of unpaid work in 2020, while men did the larger part of paid work.
73781.m: Women do the larger part of unpaid work.

73782.q: With which statistical tool does the FSO record the value of housework and family work?
73782.e: The satellite account adds to the national accounts. It values the unpaid work that is not included in GDP.
73782.m: The satellite account makes housework visible in statistics.

73783.q: Which activity counts as care work?
a: Repairing a car in a garage
Programming an app in an office
73783.e: Care work covers caring for and looking after other people, such as childcare or nursing. It is often done unpaid within families.
73783.m: Care work means caring for other people.

73784.q: What distinguishes formal from informal volunteering?
a: Formal volunteering takes place in clubs and organisations
Formal volunteering is always well paid
Informal volunteering is banned by law
73784.e: Formal volunteering is done, for example, in a sports club or for a charity. Informal volunteering is private help, such as helping neighbours or babysitting for friends.
73784.m: Formal volunteering happens in organisations, informal volunteering privately.

73785.q: Why is unpaid housework missing from gross domestic product?
a: It is not exchanged for money on markets
It is forbidden to measure it
It is already counted as a tax
73785.e: GDP mainly records work that is traded at market prices. If you cook for yourself, value is created but no sales.
73785.m: GDP does not count housework, even though it creates value.

73786.q: Which method values unpaid work at the wage an employed professional would receive for the same task?
73786.e: For cooking, for example, the market cost method uses a cook's wage. The opportunity cost method instead uses the wage the person could earn themselves.
73786.m: The market cost method values housework at professionals' wages.

73787.q: Since when has the principle of “equal pay for work of equal value” for women and men been in the Swiss Federal Constitution?
73787.e: In 1981 the people and the cantons accepted the equality article. It requires equal rights and equal pay for work of equal value.
73787.m: Equal pay has been in the constitution since 1981.

73788.q: Which law has banned discrimination at work based on sex in Switzerland since 1996?
73788.e: The Federal Act on Gender Equality came into force on 1 July 1996. It applies to hiring, pay, promotion and dismissal.
73788.m: The Gender Equality Act bans sex discrimination at work.

73789.q: From what company size have employers in Switzerland had to carry out an equal pay analysis since 2020?
73789.e: The revised Gender Equality Act requires employers with 100 or more employees to analyse their pay and have it checked.
73789.m: Larger firms must check their pay for equality.

73790.q: On which date did large nationwide women's strikes take place in Switzerland in 1991 and 2019?
73790.e: On 14 June 1991, ten years after the equality article, hundreds of thousands of women went on strike. In 2019 another big strike day followed on the same date.
73790.m: 14 June is the day of the women's strike in Switzerland.

73791.q: What does the unexplained part of the pay gap between women and men describe?
a: The part that cannot be explained by factors such as education or position
The part caused by part-time work
The part taken away by taxes
73791.e: Statisticians explain part of the pay gap with features such as education, experience or industry. The rest remains unexplained and may point to discrimination.
73791.m: The unexplained pay gap may point to discrimination.

73792.q: What does the term “glass ceiling” mean?
a: Invisible barriers to rising into leadership positions
A rule that all wages must be published
An office building with a glass roof
73792.e: The glass ceiling describes how qualified women and minorities rarely reach top positions despite their performance, even though there is no official barrier.
73792.m: The glass ceiling is an invisible limit to promotion.

73793.q: Since 2021, how much paid paternity leave have fathers in Switzerland been entitled to?
73793.e: After the popular vote in September 2020, paternity leave of two weeks has applied since 1 January 2021, financed through the income compensation scheme.
73793.m: Fathers in Switzerland receive two weeks of paternity leave.

73794.q: What is meant by horizontal segregation of the labour market?
a: Women and men mostly work in different occupations
Women only work at lower levels of the hierarchy
Work is divided up by age
73794.e: Horizontal segregation shows, for example, in the fact that care jobs are mostly chosen by women and technical jobs mostly by men. Vertical segregation concerns the levels of the hierarchy.
73794.m: Horizontal segregation means separation by field of work.

73795.q: Which principle describes the linear economic model that the circular economy wants to replace?
73795.e: In the linear economy, raw materials are extracted, made into products and thrown away after use. The circular economy wants to keep materials in circulation for as long as possible.
73795.m: The circular economy replaces throwing away with reusing.

73796.q: Which concept by Michael Braungart and William McDonough demands that products return completely to biological or technical cycles?
73796.e: Cradle to Cradle means “from the cradle to the cradle”. After use, materials should become nutrients for new products or for nature.
73796.m: Cradle to Cradle thinks of products as endless cycles.

73797.q: Which strategy comes first in the waste hierarchy?
73797.e: The waste hierarchy is: avoid, reuse, recycle, recover energy and finally dispose. The best waste is waste that is never created.

73798.q: What is it called when a higher-value product is made from waste, such as a bag from old lorry tarpaulins?
73798.e: In upcycling, waste is made into products of higher value. A well-known Swiss example is bags made from used lorry tarpaulins.
73798.m: Upcycling turns waste into something more valuable.

73799.q: What is it called when a manufacturer deliberately shortens the lifespan of a product?
73799.e: In planned obsolescence, a product is deliberately built to break or go out of date early. This goes against the circular economy.
73799.m: Planned obsolescence shortens the lifespan on purpose.

73800.q: Which British foundation is seen as one of the most important supporters of the circular economy?
73800.e: The sailor Ellen MacArthur founded the foundation in 2010. It works with companies and governments on models of the circular economy.
73800.m: The Ellen MacArthur Foundation drives the circular economy forward.

73801.q: What does the business model “Product as a Service” mean?
a: Customers rent the service, the manufacturer stays the owner
Products are given away for free
73801.e: Instead of buying a lamp, you pay for light, for example. The manufacturer then has an interest in long-lasting and repairable products.
73801.m: Whoever stays the owner builds things to last longer.

73802.q: Which waste material is collected and recycled at a rate of over 90 per cent in Switzerland?
73802.e: Over 90 per cent of glass bottles in Switzerland are collected and recycled. PET bottles and aluminium cans also have high collection rates, while mixed plastics and textiles have much lower ones.

73803.q: Which report from 1987 shaped the well-known definition of sustainable development?
a: The report to the Club of Rome
73803.e: The report “Our Common Future”, led by Gro Harlem Brundtland, defined sustainability as development that meets the needs of the present without endangering future generations.
73803.m: Sustainable means meeting today's needs without endangering future ones.

73804.q: Which three dimensions does the three-pillar model of sustainability include?
73804.e: The three-pillar model demands that the environment, the economy and society are considered at the same time. In companies this is also called the triple bottom line.
73804.m: Sustainability links the environment, the economy and society.

73805.q: How many Sustainable Development Goals does the UN's 2030 Agenda contain?
73805.e: In 2015 the UN adopted the 2030 Agenda with 17 goals (SDGs), for example on poverty, education, climate and decent work.

73806.q: Which abbreviation stands for criteria that investors use to assess environmental, social and good governance issues?
73806.e: ESG stands for Environmental, Social and Governance. Many banks and pension funds take these criteria into account when investing.
73806.m: ESG assesses environment, social issues and corporate governance.

a: A company presents itself as greener than it is
A company washes textiles in an eco-friendly way
A company pays a CO2 levy
73807.e: In greenwashing, a green image is created with advertising or vague labels without the business actually being sustainable.
73807.m: Greenwashing is a green image without green action.

73808.q: What does the yearly Earth Overshoot Day mark?
a: The day from which humanity uses more resources than the Earth can renew in a year
The hottest day of the year
The day of highest electricity use
The day of the UN climate conference
73808.e: The Global Footprint Network calculates this day every year. For years it has fallen in summer, because humanity uses far more than grows back.
73808.m: Earth Overshoot Day shows the overuse of resources.

73809.q: Which levy has Switzerland charged on fossil fuels such as heating oil since 2008?
73809.e: The CO2 levy makes heating oil and natural gas more expensive to encourage saving. A large part is returned to the population through health insurance premiums.
73809.m: The CO2 levy makes fossil fuels more expensive.

73810.q: What does the rebound effect describe?
a: Savings from efficiency are partly cancelled out by using more
Recycled material is sent back abroad
Prices rise again after a crisis
73810.e: If a car becomes more economical, people may drive more. So total consumption falls less than expected.
73810.m: Efficiency only saves if consumption does not rise.

73811.q: In which city is the International Labour Organization (ILO) based?
73811.e: The ILO, founded in 1919, is a specialised agency of the UN based in Geneva. It sets international labour standards.
73811.m: The ILO is based in Geneva.

73812.q: According to the ILO and UNICEF, how many children worldwide were affected by child labour in 2020?
73812.e: The joint estimate by the ILO and UNICEF found about 160 million children in child labour, almost half of them in dangerous work.
73812.m: Around 160 million children worldwide still work.

73813.q: Which of these is one of the ILO's core labour standards?
a: The right to your own car
A duty to work a 30-hour week
The right to work from home
73813.e: The core labour standards include freedom of association, the abolition of forced and child labour, a ban on discrimination and, since 2022, a safe and healthy working environment.
73813.m: Forced labour is banned by the ILO core labour standards.

73814.q: What is meant by a living wage?
a: A wage that covers a family's basic needs
73814.e: A living wage should cover food, housing, health, education and a small reserve. Legal minimum wages in many countries are below it.
73814.m: A living wage covers basic needs.

73815.q: Which Swiss popular initiative failed in 2020 because it did not win a majority of cantons, even though a narrow majority of the people voted yes?
73815.e: The Responsible Business Initiative wanted Swiss corporations to be liable for human rights and environmental violations abroad. On 29 November 2020 it received about 50.7 per cent yes, but not the majority of cantons.
73815.m: The Responsible Business Initiative failed on the cantons despite a popular majority.

73816.q: What does the term informal sector describe?
a: Economic activity without registration, contract or social protection
73816.e: In the informal sector, street sellers or day labourers, for example, work without an employment contract or insurance. According to the ILO, about half to two thirds of workers worldwide work informally.

73817.q: What does a Fairtrade label such as Max Havelaar mainly guarantee?
a: Minimum prices and standards for producers
73817.e: Fairtrade guarantees farming families minimum prices and an extra premium and requires social standards. Max Havelaar is the Fairtrade organisation in Switzerland.
73817.m: Fairtrade guarantees producers fair minimum prices.

73818.q: What does a collective labour agreement (GAV) regulate in Switzerland?
a: Working conditions such as wages between the social partners
The purchase contract for a machine
The rental terms of an office
73818.e: A collective labour agreement is negotiated between trade unions and employers' associations. It sets, for example, minimum wages, working hours and holidays for an industry.
73818.m: A collective labour agreement regulates working conditions in an industry.

73819.q: What is the agreement called that was meant to improve fire and building safety in textile factories in Bangladesh after the Rana Plaza collapse?
a: Accord on Fire and Building Safety
73819.e: In 2013 over 200 fashion brands and trade unions signed the legally binding Accord. Independent inspections uncovered thousands of defects.
73819.m: The Accord made textile factories in Bangladesh safer.

73820.q: According to the FSO, which form of unpaid work makes up by far the largest share of hours in Switzerland?
a: Housework such as cooking, cleaning and washing
73820.e: Household tasks make up most of the unpaid work, followed by care work. Volunteering is much smaller.
73820.m: Housework is the largest part of unpaid work.

73821.q: Which document do landlords in Switzerland very often ask for with a flat application as proof that you can pay?
a: Extract from the debt collection register
73821.e: The debt collection register extract shows whether debt collection proceedings have been started against a person. For landlords it shows whether someone pays bills reliably.
73821.m: A clean debt collection register extract improves your chances when looking for a flat.

73822.q: Within what time limit do you have to register with the residents' office in most Swiss municipalities after moving?
73822.e: Most cantons require registration with the residents' office within 14 days of moving in. The exact rules are set by the cantons and municipalities.
73822.m: After moving, you register quickly with the new municipality.

73823.q: What is the handover report, made when moving into a rented flat, for?
a: It records the condition and existing defects
It sets the amount of rent
It replaces the written tenancy agreement
It sets the amount of the rent deposit
73823.e: The report records damage and defects that already existed before moving in. That way you cannot be held liable for the previous tenant's damage when you move out.
73823.m: An exact handover report protects tenants from claims for old damage.

73824.q: What should you do if, shortly after moving in, you find defects that are missing from the handover report?
a: Report them to the landlord quickly in writing
Only mention them when moving out
Cut the rent yourself straight away
73824.e: Defects found later should be reported immediately and in writing so that they are documented. Many tenancy agreements set a short deadline for this after moving in.
73824.m: You report new defects in writing and without delay.

73825.q: How much is the radio and television fee for a private household in Switzerland per year (as of 2026)?
73825.e: Since 2025 the household fee has been 335 francs a year; it is collected by the agency Serafe. The Federal Council has decided to lower it to 312 francs for 2027.
73825.m: Every private household pays the radio and television fee, even without its own television.

73826.q: Which rooms are not counted in the number of rooms of a flat in Switzerland?
73826.e: The number of rooms includes the living rooms and bedrooms. The kitchen, bathroom, toilet and corridor are not counted; a half room is often a dining area or a kitchen-living room.
73826.m: In the number of rooms, the kitchen and bathroom do not count as rooms.

73827.q: Which rule of thumb applies to housing costs compared with net income?
73827.e: Budget advisers recommend that rent and additional costs should not be more than about a quarter to a third of net income. Otherwise too little money is left for other spending.
73827.m: Housing costs should not swallow more than about a third of your income.

73828.q: How long is the legal notice period for a flat in Switzerland?
73828.e: Under Art. 266c of the Code of Obligations, flats can be terminated with three months' notice to a locally customary date. Longer periods may be agreed in the contract, but not shorter ones.
73828.m: You give notice on a flat with at least three months' warning.

73829.q: Which legal notice period applies to a furnished room?
73829.e: For furnished rooms, Art. 266e of the Code of Obligations allows notice of two weeks to the end of a one-month rental period. This applies, for example, to many sublet rooms.
73829.m: Furnished rooms have a much shorter notice period than flats.

73830.q: Which form must the landlord use when giving notice on a flat?
a: A form approved by the canton
A text message to the tenant
73830.e: The landlord must give notice using an officially approved form (Art. 266l of the Code of Obligations). Notice without this form is void.
73830.m: A landlord can only give valid notice on a flat with the official form.

73831.q: Within what time limit can a tenant challenge the landlord's notice at the conciliation authority?
73831.e: Under Art. 273 of the Code of Obligations, the challenge must be filed with the conciliation authority within 30 days of receiving the notice. Conciliation proceedings in tenancy matters are generally free of charge.
73831.m: Anyone who wants to challenge a notice must act within 30 days.

73832.q: What is the minimum deadline for payment a landlord must give a tenant who is behind with the rent before giving notice on a flat?
73832.e: Under Art. 257d of the Code of Obligations, the landlord must set a deadline of at least 30 days in writing and warn of termination. If the tenant does not pay, notice can be given with 30 days to the end of a month.
73832.m: Tenants behind with the rent first get a payment deadline of at least 30 days.

73833.q: Who has to fix small defects in a rented flat, such as a dripping tap or a blocked drain?
a: The tenant at their own cost
73833.e: Under Art. 259 of the Code of Obligations, the tenant must remove defects that can be fixed by small cleaning jobs or repairs. The landlord must fix bigger defects.
73833.m: Small repairs in the flat are paid for by the tenant.

73834.q: How can a tenant move out without keeping to the notice period and without having to keep paying rent?
a: By proposing a reasonable replacement tenant
By simply handing in the keys
By paying two months' rent as a penalty
73834.e: Art. 264 of the Code of Obligations releases the tenant if they propose a solvent and reasonable replacement tenant who wants to take over the contract. Otherwise they must pay until the next termination date.
73834.m: Anyone moving out early needs a reasonable replacement tenant.

73835.q: How must a landlord announce a rent increase?
a: On an officially approved form with reasons
By word of mouth at the handover
By a notice in the stairwell
73835.e: Art. 269d of the Code of Obligations requires an official form with reasons, delivered at least ten days before the notice period begins. If the form or reasons are missing, the increase is void.
73835.m: A rent increase needs the official form and reasons.

73836.q: At what level was the Federal Office for Housing's mortgage reference interest rate in September 2026?
73836.e: The reference rate fell to 1.25 per cent in September 2025 and stayed at this level until at least September 2026. It is used as the basis for rent adjustments.
73836.m: The reference interest rate helps decide whether rents may rise or fall.

73837.q: By what percentage may a net rent rise at most if the reference interest rate (below 5 per cent) rises by 0.25 percentage points?
73837.e: Under Art. 13 of the tenancy ordinance (VMWG), an increase of 0.25 percentage points at a rate below 5 per cent allows a rent increase of 3 per cent. A rent of 2,000 francs could thus rise to 2,060 francs.
73837.m: If the reference rate rises by a quarter of a percentage point, the rent may rise by 3 per cent.

73838.q: A carpet with a lifespan of 10 years is damaged by the tenant after 6 years; replacing it costs 2,000 francs. What is the most the tenant has to pay?
73838.e: The tenant only pays the remaining value: after 6 of 10 years, 4/10 is left, so 2,000 times 0.4 equals 800 francs. Normal wear and tear is already covered by the rent.
73838.m: For damage, the tenant only pays the remaining value of the damaged fitting.

73839.q: What is the maximum rent deposit for a flat in Switzerland?
73839.e: Art. 257e of the Code of Obligations limits the security for homes to three months' rent. The deposit secures the landlord's claims, for example for damage or unpaid rent.
73839.m: For a flat, the deposit may be at most three months' rent.

73840.q: Where must a rent deposit paid in cash be lodged?
a: In a blocked account in the tenant's name
73840.e: The law requires it to be lodged with a bank in a savings or deposit account in the tenant's name. The landlord may not simply keep the money.
73840.m: The rent deposit belongs in a blocked account in the tenant's name.

73841.q: Who is entitled to the interest on the rent deposit account?
73841.e: The deposit account is in the tenant's name, so the interest also belongs to them. They get it back together with the deposit.
73841.m: The interest on the deposit account belongs to the tenant.

73842.q: When can a tenant ask the bank for the deposit back without the landlord's consent?
a: One year after the tenancy ends, if the landlord has made no claims
Immediately on the day of moving out
73842.e: If the landlord has not made a legal claim within one year of the end of the tenancy, the tenant can demand repayment (Art. 257e of the Code of Obligations).
73842.m: One year after moving out without claims from the landlord, you get the deposit back.

73843.q: For which rental properties does the legal maximum for the rent deposit not apply?
73843.e: Art. 257e of the Code of Obligations only limits the security when renting homes. For business premises, landlord and tenant can agree the amount freely.
73843.m: The deposit limit only protects tenants of homes.

73844.q: What is an important disadvantage of rent deposit insurance compared with a deposit account?
a: You do not get the yearly premium back
It requires a payment of ten months' rent
It only applies to business premises
73844.e: Instead of lodging money, you pay an insurer a yearly premium, which is lost. If the insurer has to pay the landlord something, it claims the amount back from the tenant.
73844.m: Deposit insurance spares your savings but costs a premium every year.

73845.q: Under what condition may the bank pay a rent deposit to the landlord?
a: With the consent of both parties or based on a legally binding decision
If the caretaker asks for it
As soon as the tenant has moved
73845.e: The bank may only release the security with the consent of both parties or based on a legally binding decision in debt collection or court proceedings (Art. 257e of the Code of Obligations).
73845.m: The landlord cannot dispose of the deposit alone.

73846.q: What applies if no additional costs are expressly agreed in the tenancy agreement?
a: They are included in the rent
The tenant must still pay them extra
They are estimated and charged yearly
73846.e: Under Art. 257a of the Code of Obligations, the tenant only has to pay additional costs if this has been specially agreed with the landlord. Otherwise they count as included in the rent.
73846.m: You only have to pay additional costs if they are listed individually in the contract.

73847.q: What does it mean if additional costs are paid “on account”?
a: You pay advances and get a statement every year
You pay a fixed amount without a statement
You only pay the costs when moving out
The landlord pays all costs himself
73847.e: With payments on account, the tenant makes monthly advance payments. Once a year the landlord draws up a statement; then there is an extra payment or a refund.
73847.m: Payments on account are advances set against the real costs every year.

73848.q: What is typical of a flat-rate charge for additional costs?
a: There is no extra payment and no refund
It is settled exactly every year
It must be approved by a court
It is only paid in winter
73848.e: With a flat rate, the tenant pays a fixed amount that should match the average values over three years. There is no statement with extra charges.
73848.m: A flat rate stays the same, however high the real costs are.

73849.q: What right does a tenant have regarding the statement of additional costs?
a: They may see the original receipts
They may draw up the statement themselves
They may cut the costs as they like
They may only check the statement after five years
73849.e: Art. 257b of the Code of Obligations gives the tenant the right to see the receipts for the statement of additional costs. That way they can check whether the amounts are correct.
73849.m: Tenants may check the receipts for the statement of additional costs.

73850.q: Which of the following costs typically belong to the additional costs of a rented flat?
73850.e: Additional costs are costs for services connected with using the flat, such as heating, hot water or cleaning the stairwell. Mortgage interest and big repairs are not included.
73850.m: Heating and hot water are the classic additional costs.

73851.q: A flat costs 1,650 francs net plus 220 francs of additional costs a month. What is the gross rent?
73851.e: The gross rent is the net rent plus additional costs: 1,650 plus 220 makes 1,870 francs.
73851.m: The gross rent includes the net rent and the additional costs.

73852.q: A tenant pays 180 francs of additional costs on account each month. The yearly statement comes to 2,400 francs. How much does he have to pay extra?
73852.e: In one year he paid 12 times 180, which is 2,160 francs, in advance. 2,400 minus 2,160 gives an extra payment of 240 francs.
73852.m: The extra payment is the difference between the real costs and the advances.

73853.q: What is the aim of billing heating costs according to use?
a: Each flat pays for what it actually uses
All flats pay exactly the same
Only the landlord pays the heating costs
Bills are only made in summer
73853.e: With heating costs billed according to use, the heat used by each flat is measured. This creates an incentive to save energy, because heating sparingly pays off directly.
73853.m: If you heat less, you pay less when billing is based on use.

73854.q: From what time does the night-time quiet period start in most Swiss house rules?
73854.e: Many house rules and municipal regulations set the night-time quiet period from 10 pm to 6 or 7 am. During this time there should be no disturbing noise.
73854.m: From 10 pm you are especially considerate in a block of flats.

73855.q: Which time is set as the midday quiet period in many house rules?
73855.e: Many house rules have a midday quiet period from about 12 to 1 pm. Noisy work such as drilling should not be done during this time.
73855.m: In many buildings you avoid noisy work over lunchtime.

73856.q: Why do house rules usually forbid leaving furniture or shoe racks in the stairwell?
a: The stairwell is an escape route
Because the municipality charges space fees
Because the post is sorted there
So the caretaker has less to clean
73856.e: Stairwells are escape and rescue routes and must be kept clear under fire safety rules. Flammable objects could become a danger in a fire.
73856.m: A clear stairwell can save lives in a fire.

73857.q: How is the use of the shared laundry room organised in many blocks of flats?
a: With a laundry rota or a booking list
73857.e: A laundry rota gives each household fixed days or times or allows bookings. That way every household can use the machines without arguments.
73857.m: The laundry rota keeps the laundry room orderly and fair.

73858.q: Which duty in the Code of Obligations is the basis for tenants having to follow the house rules?
a: The duty of care and consideration
The duty to do military service
The duty to have health insurance
73858.e: Art. 257f of the Code of Obligations requires the tenant to use the property with care and to be considerate towards other residents and neighbours. The house rules make this duty concrete.
73858.m: Tenants must live carefully and be considerate towards neighbours.

73859.q: What can the landlord do if a tenant keeps seriously disturbing the neighbours despite a written warning?
a: Give notice with 30 days to the end of a month
73859.e: If continuing the tenancy is unreasonable, Art. 257f of the Code of Obligations allows notice of at least 30 days to the end of a month after an unsuccessful warning. Taking matters into your own hands, such as cutting the power, is not allowed.
73859.m: Anyone who disturbs neighbours despite a warning risks extraordinary notice.

73860.q: Which animal may you usually keep in a rented flat even without the landlord's permission?
73860.e: Small animals such as hamsters, guinea pigs or pet birds in usual numbers count as normal use of the flat. For dogs and cats, many tenancy agreements require the landlord's consent.
73860.m: Small animals are usually allowed in rented flats; dogs and cats often need permission.

73861.q: What does joint and several liability mean if all members of a flatshare sign the tenancy agreement?
a: Each member is liable for the whole rent
Each member is only liable for their own room
Only the oldest member is liable
The municipality is liable for losses
73861.e: With joint and several liability, the landlord can demand the whole unpaid amount from any single tenant. Whoever has paid can then get the money back from the others.
73861.m: In a flatshare with a joint contract, everyone is liable for the whole rent.

73862.q: Who is liable to the landlord if in a flatshare only one person is the main tenant and the others are subtenants?
73862.e: The landlord only has a contract with the main tenant. She is liable for the whole rent and for damage, even if subtenants caused it.
73862.m: Whoever signs the main tenancy agreement alone also carries the risk alone.

73863.q: How must a joint tenancy agreement of a flatshare with several main tenants be terminated?
a: Only by the person with the biggest room
73863.e: In a joint tenancy, all tenants must sign the notice. If only one person wants to move out, an agreement with the landlord is needed.
73863.m: All tenants can only terminate a joint tenancy agreement together.

73864.q: For what reason may a landlord refuse the subletting of a room in a flatshare?
a: If the terms of the sublet are abusive
If the subtenant rides a bike
If the subtenant is a student
73864.e: The tenant needs the landlord's consent to sublet. The landlord may only refuse if the tenant does not disclose the terms, the terms are abusive or the landlord would suffer significant disadvantages (Art. 262 of the Code of Obligations).
73864.m: Subletting needs consent, which the landlord may only refuse for important reasons.

73865.q: A flatshare costs 2,400 francs rent plus 300 francs of additional costs. How much does each of three people pay if it is split equally?
73865.e: The total cost is 2,400 plus 300, which is 2,700 francs. Divided by three, that gives 900 francs per person.
73865.m: When splitting equally, you divide the gross rent by the number of people.

73866.q: How many radio and television fees does a flatshare with four people in one shared flat pay?
73866.e: The fee is charged per private household, not per person. A flatshare counts as one household and therefore only pays once.
73866.m: A flatshare pays the household fee only once.

73867.q: What do many flatshares use a shared kitty for?
a: For shared expenses such as cleaning products or basic food
73867.e: Each member regularly pays an amount into the flatshare kitty. Shared things such as cleaning products, toilet paper or spices are paid for from it.
73867.m: A flatshare kitty makes shared expenses simple and fair.

73868.q: Which damage does private liability insurance cover?
a: Damage you cause to other people
Your own medical costs after an accident
73868.e: Private liability insurance pays for damage you cause to other people or their property and defends you against unjustified claims. Your own things are not insured.
73868.m: Liability insurance pays when you cause damage to others.

73869.q: Is private liability insurance compulsory by law in Switzerland?
a: No, but many landlords require it
73869.e: Private liability insurance is not required by federal law but is strongly recommended. Many landlords ask for proof when the contract is signed.
73869.m: Private liability insurance is voluntary but highly recommended.

73870.q: Which liability insurance is required by law for all keepers in Switzerland?
73870.e: The Road Traffic Act requires liability insurance for motor vehicles. Without proof there are no number plates.
73870.m: A car may only go on the road with liability insurance.

73871.q: While cleaning, a tenant damages the washbasin in her rented flat. Which insurance usually covers this?
a: Private liability insurance with tenant's damage
73871.e: The rented flat belongs to the landlord, so to someone else. Damage to it is covered by private liability insurance, as long as tenant's damage is included.
73871.m: Damage to a rented flat is a case for private liability insurance.

73872.q: Which liability does Art. 41 of the Code of Obligations set out as the basic rule?
a: Anyone who unlawfully and culpably causes damage to another must compensate it
All damage is paid for by the state
Only companies are liable for damage
Nobody has to pay for damage under 1,000 francs
73872.e: Art. 41 of the Code of Obligations regulates fault-based liability: anyone who unlawfully causes damage on purpose or through negligence must pay compensation.
73872.m: Anyone who causes damage through their own fault must pay for it.

73873.q: Why is a dog owner liable for damage caused by their dog even if they are not at fault, unless they prove they took enough care?
a: Because liability for animal keepers is strict liability
73873.e: Art. 56 of the Code of Obligations treats animal keepers' liability as a mild form of strict liability. The keeper can only be released by proving they took all due care.
73873.m: Animal keepers are liable for their animal, even without being at fault themselves.

73874.q: What is an excess in an insurance policy?
a: The part of the damage you pay yourself
73874.e: With an excess, the insured person pays a fixed part of the damage themselves, for example 200 francs. A higher excess usually lowers the premium.
73874.m: A higher excess makes the premium cheaper.

73875.q: What does household contents insurance cover?
a: Your own movable things in case of fire, water or theft
73875.e: Household contents include all movable things, such as furniture, clothes and electronics. The insurance covers damage from fire, natural events, water and theft.
73875.m: Household contents insurance protects your own belongings.

73876.q: What does underinsurance mean in household contents insurance?
a: The sum insured is lower than the real value of the contents
You have two insurances for the same thing
You are only insured from age 25
73876.e: If the sum insured is too low, the insurer reduces the payment in proportion to the sum insured compared with the real value. That is why you should check the sum regularly.
73876.m: A sum insured that is too low leads to lower payments when damage occurs.

73877.q: Household contents worth 60,000 francs are only insured for 40,000 francs. Water damage costs 9,000 francs. How much does the insurer pay with a proportional reduction?
73877.e: Only 40,000 of 60,000 francs are insured, which is two thirds. Two thirds of 9,000 francs is 6,000 francs.
73877.m: If underinsured, you only receive the insured share of the damage.

73878.q: Which value is usually paid out by household contents insurance?
a: The purchase price ten years ago
73878.e: Most household contents insurers pay the amount you need to buy equivalent items new. That is why the sum insured is calculated with new prices.
73878.m: Household contents insurance usually works with the replacement value as new.

73879.q: What do you usually need extra cover for in household contents insurance?
a: For simple theft away from home, such as of a bike
For fire damage in the flat
For a burglary in the flat
73879.e: Burglary in the flat is included in the basic cover. Simple theft outside, such as of a locked bike at the station, usually has to be insured in addition.
73879.m: For theft while out and about you usually need extra insurance.

73880.q: Which insurance covers damage to the building itself in most cantons?
73880.e: In 19 cantons, buildings must be insured with a cantonal building insurer. The owner pays for building insurance; the tenant's contents must be insured separately.
73880.m: The owner insures the building, the residents insure the contents.

73881.q: What can the insurer do if damage was caused by gross negligence, for example by a burning candle left unattended?
a: Report the damage to the municipality
73881.e: In cases of gross negligence, the insurer may reduce its payment in proportion to the fault. Some policies waive this for an extra premium.
73881.m: Gross negligence can reduce the insurance payment.

73882.q: What are fixed costs in a household budget?
a: Expenses that come up regularly and at the same amount
Expenses for leisure and going out
Expenses you can cut at any time
73882.e: Fixed costs include rent, health insurance premiums, insurance and subscriptions. They can hardly be changed in the short term.
73882.m: Fixed costs come every month and can hardly be changed in the short term.

73883.q: Why do you plan reserves in a budget?
a: To be able to pay irregular expenses such as taxes or the dentist
73883.e: Reserves are amounts put aside each month for expenses that only come once or twice a year. That way there is no shortfall when the bill arrives.
73883.m: Reserves spread big, rare bills across all months.

73884.q: Someone expects 3,600 francs of taxes a year. How much should he put aside each month for this?
73884.e: The yearly amount is spread over twelve months: 3,600 divided by 12 gives 300 francs a month.
73884.m: In a budget you divide yearly expenses by twelve.

73885.q: A person earns 4,800 francs net a month with a 13th month's salary. What is the average monthly income over the year?
73885.e: The yearly income is 13 times 4,800, which is 62,400 francs. Divided by 12 months, that gives 5,200 francs.
73885.m: In a budget you spread the 13th month's salary over all twelve months.

73886.q: What is the difference between gross pay and net pay?
a: Social insurance contributions are deducted from gross pay
73886.e: From gross pay the employer deducts contributions for AHV, IV, EO, unemployment insurance and the pension fund, among others. Net pay is what is paid out.
73886.m: For the budget, what counts is the net pay that actually reaches your account.

73887.q: Roughly how much money do budget advisers recommend as an emergency reserve for unexpected expenses?
73887.e: A reserve of about three months' pay helps to cover unexpected expenses or a loss of income without getting into debt.
73887.m: An emergency reserve protects you from getting into debt when surprises happen.

73888.q: What can a low-income household with high health insurance premiums apply for or receive automatically from the canton?
73888.e: The cantons give people of modest means a reduction in their health insurance premiums. The conditions and procedure differ from canton to canton.
73888.m: Premium reductions help households with low incomes.

73889.q: Someone earns 6,000 francs net a month and wants to save 10 per cent. How much is that each month?
73889.e: 10 per cent of 6,000 francs is 6,000 times 0.1, which equals 600 francs.
73889.m: If you save a fixed share first, you build up savings reliably.

73890.q: What is meant by care work?
a: Caring work such as childcare and looking after relatives
73890.e: Care work means activities of caring and looking after others, such as childcare, caring for relatives and housework. A large part of it is unpaid.
73890.m: Care work includes caring for other people.

73891.q: What does the term “mental load” mean in a household?
a: The invisible burden of planning and remembering
The amount of washing per week
73891.e: Mental load describes the thinking work behind household tasks, such as remembering appointments, planning shopping and sharing out jobs. This work is often unevenly shared.
73891.m: Planning and organising in the household is work too.

73892.q: What is a chore chart in a family or flatshare for?
a: It clearly shares out household tasks among everyone
It deals with the tax return
It sets the night-time quiet period
73892.e: A chore chart shows who does which task when, such as washing up, cleaning or taking out the rubbish. That way the work is visible and fairly shared.
73892.m: A chore chart shows who does which household job.

73893.q: What does Article 163 of the Swiss Civil Code set out for married couples?
a: They provide for the family's upkeep together
Only the husband has to work
Only the wife runs the household
73893.e: Under Art. 163 of the Civil Code, spouses together provide for the family's upkeep. They agree on their contribution, for example through money, running the household or looking after the children.
73893.m: Married couples decide together how to share paid work and housework.

73894.q: From what wage must a cleaner in a private household generally be registered with the AHV (old-age insurance)?
73894.e: For work in private households, social insurance contributions are owed from the first franc. There is an exception for young people up to 25 with a small yearly wage.
73894.m: Even a cleaner in a private household must be registered with the AHV.

73895.q: Which insurance must you take out by law for an employed household helper in addition to the AHV?
73895.e: Anyone who employs someone must insure them against work accidents under the Accident Insurance Act. This also applies to household helpers working only a few hours.
73895.m: Employers in private households must insure their employees against accidents.

73896.q: According to the Federal Statistical Office, who does more housework and family work on average in Switzerland?
73896.e: Surveys by the Federal Statistical Office have shown for years that women spend more hours a week on average on housework and family work than men. For paid work it is the other way round.
73896.m: Housework and family work are still unevenly shared between the sexes in Switzerland.

73897.q: What is typical of a housing cooperative?
a: Members buy share certificates and pay a cost-based rent
The flats belong to the state
Rents follow the highest market price
You buy the flat as your property
73897.e: Cooperative members buy share certificates and rent their flat from the cooperative. The cost-based rent only covers the actual costs, without profit for investors.
73897.m: Cooperatives often offer cheaper rents because they do not need to make a profit.

a: Owning a flat with a share in the whole building
A right to a free room
73898.e: With condominium ownership, you own a co-ownership share in the property with the special right to use certain parts, such as a flat, on your own (Art. 712a of the Civil Code).
73898.m: Anyone who owns a condominium is also a co-owner of the whole building.

73899.q: Roughly what is the home ownership rate in Switzerland (as of 2021)?
73899.e: In Switzerland, only just over a third of households live in their own house or flat; in 2021 it was about 36 per cent. That gives Switzerland one of the lowest rates in Europe.
73899.m: Switzerland is a country of tenants.

73900.q: What vacancy rate for the whole of Switzerland did the Federal Statistical Office measure on 1 June 2025?
73900.e: On the reference date of 1 June 2025, about 48,000 flats were empty, which is about 1.0 per cent of the housing stock. A value below 1 per cent is often seen as a sign of a housing shortage.
73900.m: A low vacancy rate shows that flats are scarce.

a: A flat with small private units and large shared rooms
A detached house with a garden
A flat without a kitchen or bathroom
73901.e: In a cluster flat, each person or couple has a small private unit with a bathroom and often a kitchenette. On top of that there are spacious shared rooms such as a kitchen and living room.
73901.m: Cluster flats combine privacy with community.

73902.q: What did Swiss voters decide in September 2025 about the imputed rental value (Eigenmietwert)?
a: They agreed to the change of system to abolish it
They doubled the imputed rental value
73902.e: On 28 September 2025, the people and the cantons accepted the proposal that clears the way to abolishing the imputed rental value on owner-occupied homes. In return, many tax deductions disappear.
73902.m: With the 2025 vote, the change of system for the imputed rental value was decided.

73903.q: How much equity do banks usually require at least for buying a home?
a: 20 per cent of the purchase price
5 per cent of the purchase price
50 per cent of the purchase price
73903.e: Banks usually finance at most 80 per cent of the purchase price with a mortgage. At least 10 per cent must come from your own funds outside the pension fund.
73903.m: Anyone who wants to buy a house needs at least a fifth in equity.

73904.q: What does “assisted living” mean for older people?
a: Your own flat with support and emergency services
73904.e: In assisted living, older people live independently in their own flat. When needed, services such as an emergency call, cleaning or care are available.
73904.m: Assisted living combines independence with safety.

73905.q: What is the legal maximum interest rate for cash loans in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
73905.e: Since 1 January 2026 the Consumer Credit Ordinance has limited the interest on cash loans to 10 per cent; in 2025 it was still 11 per cent. For overdraft credit such as credit cards with a credit option, the limit is 12 per cent.
73905.m: Cash loans in Switzerland may cost at most 10 per cent interest.

73906.q: Within what time limit can you withdraw from a consumer credit agreement?
73906.e: Under Art. 16 of the Consumer Credit Act, the consumer can withdraw from the agreement in writing within 14 days. This way the law protects against hasty decisions.
73906.m: You can withdraw from a consumer loan within 14 days.

73907.q: What must the lender check before giving a cash loan?
a: Whether the loan can be repaid within 36 months without touching the minimum needed to live
Whether the customer owns a car
Whether the customer belongs to a club
Whether the customer has ever moved house
73907.e: The Consumer Credit Act requires a creditworthiness check: the loan must be repayable within 36 months without using the part of income that cannot be seized (Art. 28 of the Consumer Credit Act).
73907.m: A loan may only be given if it can be repaid affordably.

73908.q: Which body in Switzerland collects data on current consumer loans so that lenders can check people's debts?
73908.e: Lenders must report consumer loans to the IKO. That way other lenders can see whether a person already has loans or leasing contracts.
73908.m: The IKO helps prevent over-indebtedness from too many loans.

73909.q: Which type of contract also falls under the Consumer Credit Act?
a: The tenancy agreement for a flat
73909.e: Leasing contracts for consumer goods, such as car leasing, count as consumer credit. The creditworthiness check and the right of withdrawal apply here too.
73909.m: Leasing is legally a form of consumer credit.

73910.q: Roughly how much interest do you pay in one year on a loan of 5,000 francs at 10 per cent a year, if nothing has been repaid yet?
73910.e: 10 per cent of 5,000 francs is 5,000 times 0.1, which equals 500 francs. If you repay in instalments, the interest on the falling remaining debt is a bit lower.
73910.m: A consumer loan costs a lot of interest and makes every purchase more expensive.

73911.q: Which kind of advertising for consumer loans is banned in Switzerland?
a: Advertising that states the interest rate
73911.e: Since 2016 the Unfair Competition Act has banned aggressive advertising for consumer loans. The industry has also set its own rules, which rule out, for example, advertising aimed at young people.
73911.m: In Switzerland loans may not be advertised aggressively.

73912.q: Which document does a debtor receive as the first step of debt collection proceedings?
73912.e: After the creditor's request for debt collection, the debt collection office serves the debtor with a payment order. It asks him to pay the debt within 20 days.
73912.m: Debt collection begins with the payment order.

73913.q: Within what time limit after it is served can a debtor raise an objection in debt collection proceedings?
73913.e: Under Art. 74 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the objection must be raised within 10 days of the order being served. It stops the debt collection for the time being.
73913.m: Anyone who disputes a claim raises an objection within 10 days.

73914.q: When starting debt collection proceedings, must a creditor prove that their claim exists?
a: No, the debt collection office does not check the claim
73914.e: In Switzerland anyone can start debt collection proceedings without proving the claim. Only after an objection must the creditor prove their claim.
73914.m: Debt collection can be started without proof, which is why the objection matters.

73915.q: What must a creditor do if the debtor has raised an objection and the debt collection is to continue?
a: Have the objection set aside by a court
Simply send a second payment order
Send the police to the debtor
Nothing, the debt collection continues automatically
73915.e: The objection stops the debt collection. The creditor must show in court that the claim exists, for example with a signed acknowledgement of debt.
73915.m: After an objection, the creditor needs a court decision.

73916.q: What does a debtor always keep when their wages are seized?
a: The minimum subsistence level under debt collection law
73916.e: Only the part of income above the minimum subsistence level may be seized (Art. 93 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act). What is absolutely needed to live stays with the debtor.
73916.m: In a seizure, the minimum subsistence level stays protected.

73917.q: When does a claim backed by a certificate of unpaid debt expire?
73917.e: Under Art. 149a of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, claims from a certificate of unpaid debt expire 20 years after the certificate is issued. Until then the creditor can start debt collection again.
73917.m: A certificate of unpaid debt can follow a debtor for decades.

73918.q: For how long after proceedings have ended may third parties still see debt collection entries in the register?
73918.e: Under Art. 8a of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, third parties no longer receive information about proceedings five years after they have ended. That is why a debt collection entry can make flat hunting harder for years.
73918.m: Debt collection entries stay visible to third parties for five years.

73919.q: Since 2019, what can a person do against unjustified debt collection so that it is not disclosed to third parties?
a: Apply for non-disclosure, at the earliest after three months
73919.e: Under Art. 8a para. 3 let. d of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the debtor can apply at the earliest three months after the debt collection began. If the creditor does not show within 20 days that he has started proceedings to set aside the objection, the debt collection is no longer disclosed to third parties.
73919.m: Against unjustified debt collection there is the application for non-disclosure.

73920.q: At which debt collection office are proceedings against a private person usually started?
a: At the debtor's place of residence
At the creditor's place of residence
At the debtor's place of birth
73920.e: Under Art. 46 of the Debt Enforcement and Bankruptcy Act, the debtor is pursued at their place of residence. If the debtor moves, the office at the new place of residence is responsible.
73920.m: Debt collection happens where you live.

73921.q: You knocked over the vase by accident. What is the honest thing to do?
73921.e: Being honest means telling the truth, even when you have made a mistake. Accidents can happen to anyone.
73921.m: Owning up to a mistake is honest.

73922.q: What is it called when someone says something untrue on purpose?
73922.e: A lie is something you say that you know is not true. You want to trick others with it.
73922.m: A lie is untrue on purpose.

73923.q: You find someone else's purse in the playground. What do you do?
73923.e: Things you find belong to someone else. If you hand them in, you help the owner get them back.

73924.q: Why is honesty important for friends?
73924.e: When friends are honest, they know they can believe each other. That is how trust grows.

73925.q: Your friend cheated in a game and you saw it. What is fair and honest?
73925.e: If you calmly mention the cheating, you stay honest and fair. Laughing or cheating yourself makes it worse.
73925.m: Calmly speak up about things that are unfair.

73926.q: What often happens when you tell one lie?
73926.e: One lie often leads to more lies so that it isn't found out. That quickly becomes tiring.
73926.m: One lie often leads to more lies.

73927.q: Which sentence is honest if you forgot your homework?
73927.e: Only the first sentence says what really happened. The other sentences are not true.
73927.m: Honest means saying what really happened.

a: A reason that isn't quite true
73928.e: With an excuse, you try to talk your way out of something. The reason you give is often not true.
73928.m: An excuse distracts from the truth.

73929.q: What makes someone a good friend?
73929.e: Good friends support each other, even when things are difficult. They are there for each other.

73930.q: Your friend is sad. What can you do?
73930.e: Asking shows that the other person matters to you. Often just listening helps.

73931.q: A new child is in the class and doesn't know anyone. What is kind?
a: Copy them to make fun of them
73931.e: New children often feel unsure. An invitation to play helps them fit in.
73931.m: New children are happy to be invited.

73932.q: Can you be friends with more than one child?
a: No, only with children from your own class
No, only with your own brothers and sisters
73932.e: You can have lots of friends. Every friendship is something special.
73932.m: You can have lots of friends.

73933.q: Your friend tells you a secret that doesn't harm anyone. What do you do?
a: Write it down and hand it out
73933.e: Keeping a secret shows that you can be trusted. Then your friend can tell you things later on too.

73934.q: Which kind of secret should you tell an adult you trust?
73934.e: Secrets where someone is afraid or being hurt can and should be told to someone you trust. That is not betrayal.

73935.q: How do you show a friend that you like them?
73935.e: Spending time together shows that someone matters to you. Playing, talking and laughing make a friendship stronger.

73936.q: Your friend made a mistake while drawing and is sad. What do you say?
73936.e: Encouraging words comfort your friend and show that you are on her side. Everyone makes mistakes.
73936.m: Good friends cheer each other up.

73937.e: A compliment is a friendly remark, for example “You've drawn that really well”. It makes others happy.

73938.q: You have three apples and your friend has none. What is kind?
73938.e: When you share, you think of others too. Then you both have something.

73939.q: You share 8 jelly sweets fairly with a friend. How many does each of you get?
73939.e: 8 divided by 2 is 4. That way you each have the same number.
73939.m: When you share fairly, everyone gets the same amount.

73940.q: Two children want the same swing. What is a good solution?
73940.e: Taking turns is a way of sharing. Everyone gets a go.

73941.q: Apart from things, what else can you share?
73941.e: You can also share time, ideas and joy with others. That costs nothing.
73941.m: You can share time and joy too.

73942.q: Can you just take something that belongs to someone else to share it?
a: Yes, if the owner is away
73942.e: Sharing something that isn't yours is only OK with permission. Otherwise you are taking something away from someone.
73942.m: Only share other people's things with permission.

73943.q: You cut a pizza into 4 equal pieces for 4 children. How many pieces does each child get?
73943.e: 4 pieces for 4 children is 1 piece per child. That is fair.
73943.m: The same number of pieces is fair.

73944.q: How do you politely ask if you can borrow something?
73944.e: Saying “please” is asking politely. Then the other person can decide for themselves.

73945.q: What do you do with a borrowed book?
73945.e: Borrowed things belong to someone else. You look after them well and give them back.

73946.q: In a race, one child starts too early. Is that fair?
a: No, everyone should start at the same time
Yes, fast people can start earlier
Yes, if they really want to win
73946.e: Starting too early gives you an unfair advantage. Everyone should start running at the same time.
73946.m: In a fair race, everyone starts at the same time.

73947.q: How does a fair winner behave?
73947.e: If you win and stay friendly, you don't hurt anyone. Laughing at others spoils the fun for everyone.

73948.q: What is fair behaviour in sport called?
73948.e: Fair play means keeping to the rules and respecting your opponent.

73949.q: How can you fairly decide who starts in a game?
73949.e: When you roll a dice, every child has the same chance. That is fair.
73949.m: Rolling a dice gives everyone the same chance.

73950.q: A child can't run because of a plaster cast. What is fair in the game?
73950.e: Being fair sometimes means being considerate. With a suitable job, the child can still join in.
73950.m: Fair is when everyone can join in.

73951.q: What is a foul in football?
73951.e: A foul is breaking the rules of the game, for example tripping someone up. There is a penalty for it.
73951.m: A foul is against the rules.

73952.q: A child has fallen over and is crying. What do you do?
73952.e: Helpful people look after others when they need help. If someone is hurt, you fetch an adult.
73952.m: Someone who falls over needs help.

73953.q: Who do you call on 144 in Switzerland after a bad accident?
73953.e: In Switzerland, 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service, the rescue service with the ambulance.
73953.m: You reach the ambulance service on 144.

73954.q: What is the emergency number for the fire brigade in Switzerland?
73954.e: In Switzerland you reach the fire brigade on 118. You call them, for example, if there is a fire.

73955.q: Which number can children in Switzerland call when they are worried?
73955.e: The number 147 from Pro Juventute is there for children and young people. Someone listens and helps there, day and night and free of charge.
73955.m: When you're worried, the number 147 helps.

73956.q: An older man is carrying heavy bags up the stairs. What is helpful?
73956.e: If you first ask whether help is wanted, you are helpful and polite. The other person can then say yes or no.
73956.m: Offer help in a friendly way.

73957.q: How can you help at home?
73957.e: Small jobs like laying the table help the whole family. Then one person doesn't have to do everything alone.

73958.q: What do you say when someone has helped you?
73958.e: Saying “thank you” shows that you value the help. That makes the helper happy.

73959.q: How does a child who is laughing and jumping feel?
73959.e: Laughing and jumping are typical signs of joy.
73959.m: Someone who laughs is often happy.

73960.q: A child has tears in their eyes and their head is hanging down. How do they probably feel?
73960.e: Tears and a hanging head often show sadness. You can ask what is wrong.

73961.q: A child is clenching their fists and has a red face. What feeling do they probably have?
73961.e: Clenched fists and a red face are often signs of anger. You can ask the child what is wrong.

73962.q: What can help when you are very angry?
73962.e: Breathing deeply calms the body. Afterwards you can say better what is bothering you.
73962.m: Deep breaths calm you down when you're angry.

73963.q: What is the feeling called when you are frightened of something?
73963.e: Fear warns us about dangers. It is good to talk to someone about it.

73964.q: You have finished painting a difficult picture. Which feeling fits?
73964.e: When you have managed something difficult, you are proud of it.
73964.m: When you've managed something, you're proud.

73965.q: What is it called when you can feel what others are feeling?
73965.e: Empathy means you sense how someone else is feeling. Then you can help better.

73966.q: What is the feeling called when you want something that someone else has?
73966.e: You feel envy when you begrudge someone something or want it yourself. Everyone has this feeling sometimes.

73967.e: All feelings are allowed, including anger and sadness. What matters is how you deal with them.

73968.q: What helps most when two children are arguing?
73968.e: When you talk to each other, you understand what is bothering the other person. That way you find a solution.

73969.q: How do you start a sentence to say what bothers you without blaming someone?
73969.e: An “I” sentence says how you feel without attacking the other person. That way the other person listens better.

73970.q: What should you do while the other person explains in an argument?
73970.e: If you listen, you find out why the other person is upset. Then it's your turn.

73971.q: What is a solution called where both sides give in a little?
73971.e: In a compromise, everyone gets some of what they want. So in the end both are fairly happy.
73971.m: In a compromise, both give in.

73972.q: Who can help if children can't sort out their argument on their own?
73972.e: Teachers or parents can help find a solution. In some schools, trained children also help as “peacemakers”.
73972.m: In a difficult argument, get help.

73973.q: What is not a good idea in an argument?
73973.e: Violence hurts and makes the argument worse. Talking, listening or taking a break help.

73974.q: Why can a short break help in an argument?
73974.e: With a bit of distance, you get calmer. Afterwards you usually talk to each other in a friendlier way.
73974.m: A break helps everyone calm down.

73975.q: What is a person called who helps two people who are arguing to sort things out?
73975.e: A mediator helps both sides listen to each other and find a solution. They don't take sides.

73976.q: Two children want to read the same book. Which solution is peaceful?
73976.e: If both read together, both get something out of it. That way there is no argument.

73977.q: You bumped into someone by accident. What do you say?
73977.e: You say sorry even if it was an accident. That way the other person knows it wasn't on purpose.

73978.q: What is part of a good apology?
73978.e: If you apologise properly, you say what you did wrong. That shows you are sorry.

73979.q: Apart from words, how can you show you are sorry?
73979.e: If, for example, you build a tower back up after knocking it over, you put the damage right. That shows you mean it.
73979.m: Putting things right shows you are sorry.

73980.q: Someone apologises to you. What can you answer?
73980.e: Accepting an apology ends the argument. Afterwards you can play together again.

73981.q: What is it called when you no longer hold a mistake against someone?
73981.e: Forgiving means letting go of being angry. That does both people good.
73981.m: Forgiving means letting go of anger.

73982.q: What would be a bad apology?
73982.e: If you blame the other person in the same sentence, you aren't really apologising. A real apology has no “but”.

73983.q: What is it called when two people become friends again after an argument?
73983.e: When two people make up, they put their argument behind them. It often starts with an apology.
73983.m: After the argument comes making up.

73984.q: When is the best time to apologise?
a: Only when the other person asks for it
73984.e: The sooner you apologise, the sooner the anger is over.

73985.e: If you let others finish speaking, you show that their opinion matters. That is respectful.
73985.m: Letting people finish speaking is respectful.

73986.q: What do people in German-speaking Switzerland often say as a greeting?
73986.e: “Grüezi” is a common, polite greeting in German-speaking Switzerland. Greeting people shows respect.

73987.q: How do you treat other people's things respectfully?
73987.e: Other people's things belong to someone else. You handle them carefully.

73988.q: How do you show respect for nature?
73988.e: If you take your rubbish with you, you protect animals and plants. That way nature stays beautiful.
73988.m: Take your rubbish home from nature.

73989.q: A child doesn't want to be hugged. What is respectful?
73989.e: Everyone can decide for themselves who may touch them. A no must be respected.

73990.q: How do you show respect for animals?
73990.e: Animals have feelings too and can feel pain. You treat them kindly and carefully.

73991.q: What is respectful on the bus?
a: Putting your feet on the seat
73991.e: Older or injured people often find it hard to stand. Offering them your seat shows respect.

73992.e: Swear words hurt others. Respectful people don't use them.

73993.q: Why are there rules at school?
a: So that everyone gets on well together
73993.e: Rules help everyone treat each other safely and fairly. Without rules there would be more arguments.

73994.q: At which colour of traffic light can you cross the road as a pedestrian?
73994.e: At green, pedestrians may cross. At red, you have to wait.

73995.q: What do you do in Switzerland before crossing a zebra crossing?
73995.e: “Wait, look, listen, walk” (in Swiss German “Warte, luege, lose, laufe”) is the Swiss road safety rule for children. You wait, look, listen and only then cross.
73995.m: Before crossing, wait, look and listen.

73996.q: How do you show in class that you want to say something?
73996.e: If you put your hand up, you wait until it's your turn. That way everyone can talk in peace.
73996.m: If you want to say something, put your hand up.

73997.q: Who can make rules together in a class?
73997.e: Many classes have a class council. There, children and the teacher discuss rules together.
73997.m: In the class council, you make rules together.

73998.q: What often happens when nobody keeps to the rules of a game?
73998.e: Rules make sure everyone knows what applies. Without them, people argue.

73999.q: What is best to wear for your safety when cycling?
73999.e: A bike helmet protects your head if you fall. That is why it is very important.
73999.m: A bike helmet protects your head.

74000.q: What are rules called that apply to everyone in a country?
74000.e: Laws are the rules of a country. In Switzerland, parliaments pass laws, and sometimes the people vote on them too.
74000.m: Laws apply to everyone in the country.

74001.q: Which rule usually applies when playing ball in the playground?
74001.e: If nobody hits anyone on purpose, nobody gets hurt. Everyone should have fun.
74001.m: When playing, never hurt anyone on purpose.

74002.q: A child speaks a different language at home. What is right?
74002.e: In Switzerland, many families speak a different language at home. Knowing several languages is a treasure.
74002.m: Knowing several languages is a treasure.

74003.q: A child uses a wheelchair. What is kind when playing?
a: Find a game they can join in
74003.e: With a bit of imagination, you can find games that everyone can join in. Nobody should be left out.

74004.q: Why is it good that people are different?
